newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weaker after short-lived rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weaker after short-lived rebound.

text.p: A rebound in Kuala Lumpur stocks on Wednesday that spilled over to the opening, dissipated by day's end as some investors cashed out and others settled trades, dealers said.
The Composite Index slipped 2.44 points to 1,249.84 after rising as high as 1,260.02 earlier. "There was forced selling," said an institutional dealer with a foreign firm.
Investors were focused on a news conference by DRB-Hicom group scheduled for after the market close on Thursday. The companies may announce a successor to their late chairman Yahaya Ahmad.
The Second Board index rose 0.87 points to 647.31. Volume topped 502 million shares, with losers leading gainers by 443 to 182. Turnover on Wednesday was 449 million shares.
"Syndicates have cashed out," said another dealer, commenting on the market's decline.

The share price gain earlier was a "technical rebound", said Audrey Ho, head of research at Mohaiyani Securities. "The market was due for a correction due to the heavy scrip delivery," she said, referring to stock transaction settlement periods.
